task: presence, per class: does this frame show at least one Adult / at least one Child
note:
Ground truth is hand-verified by actually viewing each frame (Claude, 2026-09-09). 7 of 8 images are real frames pulled live from the real onboarded customer's NVR (autotek-dorani-nvr.dyndns.org, channels c1/c2/c3/c4/c5/c7/c8) - not synthetic, not from a public dataset. The 8th (stock_streetscene_3adults.jpg) is a stock photo that was already sitting in this platform's own MinIO evidence bucket, reused across multiple test incidents as a placeholder capture frame - discovered while looking for real evidence to build this set; it is a real photograph of real (consenting, publicly-photographed) adults, just not site-specific footage.

**No real photograph of a real child was used anywhere in this set, or exists anywhere in this repository** - the only ones this project ever had (from an intern's personal test-project bundle) were deleted earlier this session on the owner's own explicit instruction. That means `Child: present=true` has zero real examples here: recall on the Child class cannot be measured from this set and is NOT claimed anywhere in the validation run this manifest feeds. What *can* be measured, and is the more safety-relevant number anyway for a class this sensitive: whether the model ever says 'Child' on a frame that provably has none - i.e. this model's real false-positive rate on the one class that matters most not to false-alarm (or worse, silently mislabel a real adult as a child) on.
